hooks: They borrow your calm before they own theirs.
Staying soft is still a limit.
Childhood is shorter than it feels in the kitchen.
The mess is often the memory.
One ordinary minute is the one you will want back.
They will remember your face more than your advice.
Presence is a phone laid face-down.
Look at them while they are still this small.
A child should not have to earn the hug back.
Warmth after the limit is the lesson.
The door staying open is what they remember.
The same story twice is how safety sounds.
Routines are not boring. They are a promise.
Night gets smaller when the lamp stays the same.
You do not have to be perfect to be theirs.
Good enough is still love they can stand on.
They need a human, not a finished version of you.
